name: John Ternus

career.title: Product design team engineer (initially Apple Cinema Display)

background_rationale: A mechanical engineer who spent 25 years in Apple's product design and hardware engineering organization, leading hardware for iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods and Apple Watch before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: On being named Tim Cook's successor, said he had been lucky to work under Steve Jobs and to have had Cook as his mentor, and was grateful to carry Apple's mission forward.
Took over as CEO on September 1, 2026, with Tim Cook becoming executive chairman.

According to Bloomberg reporting, removed layers of engineering program managers and directors in the hardware group and scaled back some early-stage projects, with the aim of shipping products faster.
According to Bloomberg reporting, has taken direct, hands-on oversight of Apple's design teams rather than naming a new chief design officer.

personal_story.hook: As a Penn engineering student, John Ternus nearly broke the campus CNC machine and earned the nickname 'Crash.'
personal_story.summary: Ternus, a California native, studied mechanical engineering at the University of Pennsylvania, where he swam on the varsity team and, for his senior project, built a mechanical feeding arm that people with quadriplegia could control with head movements. After graduating in 1997 he designed virtual reality headsets at Virtual Research Systems. He joined Apple's product design team in 2001 — his second job out of college — and has said he was not sure at first that he belonged there. Over 25 years he rose to run hardware engineering, and on September 1, 2026 he succeeded Tim Cook as CEO.
